main_text.p: dunt, frustulo & cultello; Quin stet nobis cum Nazian-zeno eiusmodi πάντα συλλογον φεύγειν ὑπονοίᾳ πολλῶν; ὃν μηδεμίας (πιστεύσῃς nimi-rum) συνόδῳ πλὴν χρηστόν. μηδὲ λύειν κα-τὰν μέλλον ἐκκλησίας ἢ αἱρετικὴν: Concili-um a cilijs oculorum memini dictum Isidoro; quod in vnum omnes dirigant mentis obtu-tum; concilium ergo agere non possunt, qui publicam vsquequaq; dissidentiam pro-fitentur: Frustra nos hoc ten-tabimus, nisi illorum quisque apud se domi pacem meditari occœperit, animumque indu-xerit, abiecto omni præiudi-cio, ac pertinaci partium stu-dio, veritati (vbi illa semel af-fulserit)

page.notes: Greek text in the main column is printed in Greek letters; transcription of the Greek is approximate. Marginal note at right: "Isid. in præf. Concil. Bin." The faint text at the far left edge is show-through and was left out. The word "fulserit)" at the foot is the catchword and is also given above in the text.
